Irene — technical summary below, short and actionable. Attachment: retention-matrix-v3.xlsx (updated by infra).

- Immutable snapshots: we can enforce object-lock (S3 WORM) for customer backup buckets. Configurable TTL on immutable snapshots up to 365 days; 90 days is fully supported.
- Purge pipeline: destruction jobs are executed in a staged workflow: mark-for-delete -> escrow/freeze -> final-delete. The scheduled job that moves items from escrow to final-delete runs at 02:00 UTC by default and can be shifted within a maintenance window.
- Escrow/Hold: we support a 14-day escrow hold where items are not destructible but flagged for final-delete. During escrow, automatic restores are blocked unless a legal/ops override is submitted (we log overrides to audit).
- Subprocessor notification: we can generate automated notification emails to listed contacts and also emit a webhook event to an integration endpoint. The subprocessor-notify-template.docx is our standard. Default notice lead time is 30 days; we can make this a contractual SLA.
- Operational caveat: if Veridian opts into immutable WORM at bucket-level, it will block object overwrite/modify for the lock period; any emergency data corrections require an internal privileged procedure and will be logged/audited.

Proposed immediate response: confirm 90d immutability + 30d subproc notice + 14d escrow. I'll queue a config change and produce an implementation checklist for the first week (retention labels, subproc list, webhook endpoint test).

Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear ask and for the matrix. Short summary and proposed contractual language below.

Summary (what Redwood can commit to right away):
- Immutable snapshot window: 90 days (object-lock/WORM) on customer backup buckets.
- Subprocessor & customer notifications: 30 days prior written notice to the Customer and to listed subprocessors. Notifications can be sent via email and webhook.
- Escrow (non-destructive staging) window: 14 days between mark-for-delete and final destruction to allow for restores or legal holds.
- Emergency overrides: available but require dual-approval (ops + legal) and will be logged; Veridian will receive an audit notification within 24 hours of any override.

Proposed addendum excerpt (for legal):
"Redwood shall provide an immutable snapshot window of ninety (90) days for Backups generated by or on behalf of Customer. Prior to any permanent deletion of Backups, Redwood shall provide thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer and to the Customer's listed subprocessors. Upon issuance of such notice, Redwood will place Backups into a non-destructive escrow staging period for fourteen (14) calendar days prior to final destruction. Emergency restoration or deletion overrides shall be subject to Redwood's internal dual-approval procedure and will be auditable by Customer."

I've attached the draft DPA addendum and the subprocessor notification template for your review. If this language looks good, Markus will route the DocuSign and we can aim to have the addendum signed within 5 business days. Karthik will kick off config changes once we receive the signed addendum and a subprocessor list/notification endpoint.
